description: Canonical catalog of GLOBAL defects. One authoritative definition per defect, shared by every part. scope='all' defects are checked on every part unless a part explicitly excludes them. scope='opt_in' defects are only checked when a part lists them under global_defects.include_opt_in.

corrosion.signature: Brown/orange/red mottled rust or oxidation staining on any surface, wall, face or edge. Distinguish from plating tint or shadow - true corrosion has a rough, blotchy texture and warm colour.
disambiguation: DECISIVE TEST vs edge_chip at a rim/edge: corrosion is reddish/brown/orange mottled OXIDATION STAINING on INTACT metal - the surface/contour is unbroken, no material is missing.

If the reddish colour sits ON A SHEARED, CHIPPED or NOTCHED rim/edge where MATERIAL IS MISSING or torn (a break in the smooth edge outline), that is an EDGE_CHIP (the reddish is just contact/scuff staining on the chip), NOT corrosion.
Judge the EDGE OUTLINE first: smooth intact edge + reddish stain -> corrosion; broken/sheared edge with reddish scuff -> edge_chip.

line_mark.signature: A thin, continuous linear trace running across the surface where the finish has been rubbed or gouged away, often spanning a large fraction of the part length and crossing over holes or markings WITHOUT breaking. It may catch the light as a bright hairline OR read as a relatively FAINT continuous line - do NOT assume the defect is the brightest streak on the part. On a brushed/plated finish it is distinguished from the normal directional grain by being a SINGLE, more-defined, continuous groove that holds ONE unbroken path over a large fraction of the part (often running hole-to-hole), whereas grain and polishing streaks are many short, shallow, look-alike parallel lines (see FINISH GRAIN RULE). Continuity and singularity matter more than orientation or brightness. A DARK or near-black mark is NOT a line_mark even if elongated - that is a dark_spot / dark_mark.
finish_grain_rule: DECISIVE TEST vs the normal BRUSHED-FINISH GRAIN: a brushed or plated metal surface is naturally covered in many fine, roughly PARALLEL directional grain lines and shallow polishing micro-scratches - these are the FINISH, not defects.

Do NOT pick the single brightest hairline just because it is shiny; on a brushed finish the brightest hairlines are usually grain/polish, and the genuine line_mark may run at a SIMILAR angle to the grain, so angle alone does NOT separate them.

Identify the line_mark by being a SINGLE, more-defined, CONTINUOUS groove that stands apart from the grain field: it holds one unbroken path over a large fraction of the part (frequently connecting or crossing the holes) and is slightly deeper/more distinct than the surrounding shallow grain, EVEN WHEN it is relatively FAINT rather than the brightest thing on the part.
Judge by CONTINUITY, singularity and definition, not by maximum brightness.
A bright hairline that is short, one of many look-alike parallel streaks, and indistinguishable from the surrounding grain field is finish grain, NOT a line_mark.
enumeration_rule: ENUMERATE EVERY DISTINCT LINE MARK - a part often has SEVERAL, and MISSING a faint one is the most common line_mark error.

(1) FIRST sweep the whole face and make a COUNT of every distinct groove you can see - do not stop at the most obvious/brightest one; deliberately look for additional FAINTER grooves at other positions and angles, including short ones and ones near an edge or a hole.
(2) THEN draw EACH counted groove as its OWN tight box in `bbox`, so the number of boxes equals the number of grooves you counted.

CRITICAL: the 0.60 confidence gate and the 'prefer OK over a false flag' bias govern the DECISION on an individual mark's certainty - they are NOT a licence to silently DROP a faint groove you can actually see.
A faint but genuinely visible groove is reported with a LOWER confidence (or the whole result set to NEEDS_REVIEW if you are unsure), NEVER omitted.
Under-counting (reporting one line when several exist) is a FAILURE even if the one you reported is correct.
When two grooves are close and parallel, they are still TWO separate marks - box both, do not merge them into one.
confidence_rule: SCORE CONFIDENCE BY HOW MUCH CLEARLY-VISIBLE CONTINUOUS GROOVE THERE IS = CONTINUITY x LENGTH, *NOT* by peak brightness.

A line_mark's confidence must reflect the amount of unbroken, plainly-visible groove: a LONG groove that stays clearly visible end-to-end (e.g. running hole-to-hole across most of the part) is HIGH confidence; a SHORT groove, or one that fades out / is only visible over part of its span (especially where it crosses a bright, highly-reflective zone), is LOW confidence.

Do NOT reward a short mark just because one spot on it is very bright or 'pops' against a dark/mottled patch - local brightness or high local contrast on a noisy background does NOT make it a confident line_mark.
Concretely, when comparing two marks: the one whose visible continuous length (fraction of the part it clearly spans) is greater gets the HIGHER confidence, even if the other has a brighter peak.
Faint-but-long and clearly continuous beats short-and-locally-bright.
For a part with several grooves, more total visible groove length across them means higher overall confidence.
specular_rejection_rule: REJECT SPECULAR REFLECTION AND RIM GLARE - the most common line_mark FALSE POSITIVE on a shiny plated part.

The BRIGHTEST, boldest long bright band on a polished face is almost always a mirror-like SPECULAR REFLECTION (a broad bright stripe down the part), NOT a line_mark; and a bright band that runs ALONG or just inside the part's EDGE/silhouette is RIM GLARE, also not a defect.

A genuine line_mark is FAINTER and LOWER-CONTRAST than these bright bands: a thin, subtle continuous groove on the matte brushed face, set IN from the silhouette and distinct from the dominant reflection stripe.
NEVER pick the single brightest, boldest or longest bright band as the line_mark - the real marks are the low-contrast grooves you only notice on close inspection.
If a candidate coincides with the part outline, or is the dominant central reflection band, REJECT it and look instead for the fainter interior grooves.
zoom_rule: ZOOM BEFORE YOU CONCLUDE - a faint line_mark is often INVISIBLE at full-frame scale and only becomes obvious when magnified.
Do NOT decide 'no line_mark' (or miss one) from the whole-part view alone.

Sweep the face in overlapping REGIONS and mentally ZOOM into each suspect band as if it filled the frame, especially the matte interior away from the bright reflection stripe; a ~1px groove at full-frame size becomes a clear line when zoomed.

This is the decisive step for FAINT grooves: if a groove is only ambiguously visible zoomed-out, ZOOM IN before reporting present/absent - many real marks are missed purely because the inspector never magnified the region.
When still visible-but-uncertain after zooming, use the DIRECTION-UNCERTAIN FALLBACK (region bbox + NEEDS_REVIEW), never silent omission.
disambiguation: DECISIVE TEST vs dark_spot / dark_mark: judge by COLOUR FIRST, then shape.

A line_mark is a BRIGHT / SILVER / shiny metallic hairline - a scratch or groove where the surface finish has been rubbed or gouged away exposing lighter, shinier BARE METAL that catches the light as a fine bright line.
Its defining trait is that it is LIGHTER and shinier than the surrounding finish.
A mark that is DARK or near-BLACK is NOT a line_mark even when it is elongated or streaky - a dark or black elongated mark is a dark_spot or dark_mark.
Classify by colour first: only bright / metallic exposed-metal scratches are line_marks; anything dark or black goes to dark_spot / dark_mark.
DECISIVE TEST vs dent: a line_mark is FLAT with no depth - a thin continuous surface trace with NO shadow trough beside it.

A DENT is a 3D deformation whose bent/raised edge also catches light as a bright glint, but that glint is SHORT, ROUNDED and LOCALISED (often on a rim/edge/collar) and sits next to a SHADOWED depression, and the contour is broken.
If the bright mark is localised, curved, on an edge, or paired with a depression -> dent, NOT line_mark.
Only a thin, continuous, depth-less bright streak is a line_mark.

annotation.instruction: This defect is drawn as a BOX, not a line. For every distinct line mark / scratch on the part, emit one tight box per distinct line mark: a `bbox` [x,y,w,h] normalized (0..1, whole-image, DISPLAY orientation) that encloses just that one groove plus a thin margin - keep it TIGHT to the groove, never a box spanning the whole face. ENUMERATE EVERY DISTINCT LINE MARK: if the part shows 4 scratches, emit 4 boxes so the count matches; do NOT merge several grooves into one big box and do NOT report only the most obvious one. If a groove is faint or its extent is ambiguous, still emit a tight box around the visible groove region, give it a LOWER confidence, and set the overall result to NEEDS_REVIEW - never omit a visible groove.

confidence_model.formula: confidence = 0.45*continuity + 0.35*length + 0.20*distinctness (each factor 0..1, judged BY EYE; the formula only COMBINES them). Matches confidence_rule: score by CONTINUITY x LENGTH, not brightness.

continuity.meaning: how UNBROKEN the groove is end-to-end (1.0 = one continuous path; low = broken/dashed/only partly visible).

length.meaning: how much of the part the clearly-visible groove SPANS (1.0 = runs hole-to-hole across most of the part; low = short).

distinctness.meaning: how clearly it stands APART from the brushed grain / specular streaks (1.0 = one defined groove; low = blends into grain).

dent.signature: Metal pushed in or deformed but intact - no missing material. Any localised edge, rim, collar, flange or face deformation that breaks the smooth expected contour.
disambiguation: DECISIVE TEST vs line_mark: a dent is a 3D DEFORMATION (metal pushed in, contour broken) - its edge may catch light as a bright glint, but it is SHORT, ROUNDED, LOCALISED and paired with an adjacent SHADOWED depression.
A line_mark is a FLAT, thin, continuous, depth-less bright streak with no shadow trough.
Judge by DEPTH/SHAPE: localised + depression + broken contour -> dent; thin continuous flat line -> line_mark.
In multi-part collages, zoom into the region before deciding - a small dent reads as a bright streak at collage scale.

edge_chip.signature: A clean cut, sheared notch or chipped-away section on an outer edge/flange where material is MISSING - a straight or angular break in an otherwise smooth silhouette. Missing material distinguishes this from a dent.
localization: BBOX MUST tightly enclose ONLY the actual chipped/sheared notch on the edge (the spot where material is missing, plus a thin margin) - NOT the whole rim arc and NOT a generic corner of the part frame.

Localize to the exact break in the silhouette: include any bright torn/rough metal AND any reddish contact/scuff marks that mark the damaged patch, and make sure the box is CENTRED on them (do not let it drift to one side and clip part of the damage).
The chip is usually small - well under ~0.15 of the image in each dimension.
Coordinates are in DISPLAY orientation (the image as shown).

dark_mark.signature: A larger or elongated irregular ABSOLUTE-DARK (near-black) blemish, smudge, streak-like blotch or clustered contamination with defined but non-geometric boundaries - a genuinely dark, near-black area, not merely a dull or tinted area. Use dark_mark when the dark material forms a connected patch/cluster or elongated smear larger than an isolated speck; there may be ONE or MULTIPLE such areas, and each gets its own box.
false_positive_rule: The rainbow / passivation plating TINT (purple / pink / green / gold iridescence) is the FINISH, NOT a dark_mark - NEVER mark the tint even though it is coloured.
If a region is merely coloured, dull, or slightly shadowed but NOT near-black, do not flag it.
Only a clearly near-black patch counts.
localization: BBOX MUST enclose ONLY the near-black blemish itself (plus a thin margin), tight on the dark pixels - not the surrounding tint, not the whole face.
Each near-black area gets its OWN tight box (emit several dark_mark entries when several exist).
The blemish is usually small - typically well under ~0.15 of the image in each dimension.
The marker segments the actual dark pixels inside this bbox, so keep the box tight on the darkened area.
classification_rule: CLASSIFY BY CONNECTED AREA AND SHAPE: a connected elongated smear, irregular patch, or cluster of touching dark pixels is dark_mark even when narrow; reserve dark_spot for separate small isolated specks.
Do not split one connected dark mark into several dark_spot boxes.

darkness.meaning: how near-BLACK the blemish is vs merely tinted/shadowed (1.0 = clearly near-black; low = only dull/tinted).

boundary_definition.meaning: how discrete and clearly-bounded the blotch is (1.0 = crisp edge; low = diffuse/hazy).

not_tint_certainty.meaning: confidence it is a REAL dark mark, NOT passivation tint / glare / shadow.

dark_spot.signature: Small, DISCRETE, separated, roughly rounded dark specks on the surface, clearly darker than the surrounding finish but smaller and less connected than a dark_mark. A part OFTEN has SEVERAL (commonly 2 or more), and they frequently sit near or ON the strap EDGES as well as on the open face - not only in the centre. Do not use dark_spot for one connected elongated smear, irregular patch, or touching cluster; those are dark_mark.
enumeration_rule: ENUMERATE EVERY DISTINCT dark spot - UNDER-COUNTING is the most common error.
Sweep the WHOLE face AND both long edges, COUNT each discrete spot, and emit ONE tight bbox PER spot (several dark_spot entries when several exist).
Do NOT collapse multiple spots into one big box, and do NOT report only the single most obvious one.
false_positive_rule: NOT a dark_spot: the uniform rainbow / passivation plating TINT, a HOLE bore or its shadow, specular glare, or faint DIFFUSE haze / mottling with no clear boundary.
A dark_spot is a DISCRETE, clearly-bounded darker blemish - if there is no crisp darker spot standing out from the finish, do NOT flag one (prefer OK).
actionability_rule: TINY-SPECK GATE: do not annotate an isolated one- or few-pixel dark dot when it has no clearly visible surrounding footprint or boundary.
Treat that evidence as below 0.60 confidence and leave it unmarked.
Annotate only when the dark evidence forms a visibly coherent, defect-sized area with a boundary; the bbox should cover that full visible footprint, not individual dark pixels.
disambiguation: DECISIVE TEST vs line_mark: judge by COLOUR FIRST.
A dark_spot is any mark that is DARKER (near-black) than the surrounding finish.
If the mark is dark or black, classify it as a dark_spot (or a dark_mark when it is a larger solid blotch) EVEN IF it is somewhat elongated or streaky - darkness wins over shape.
A line_mark is reserved for BRIGHT / silver / shiny metallic scratches where bare metal is exposed; never label a dark or near-black mark as a line_mark.
Escalate to dark_mark when the dark area is a larger solid blotch rather than one or a few small dark spots.
classification_rule: CLASSIFY BY CONNECTED AREA AND SHAPE AFTER THE COLOUR TEST: emit one dark_spot per separate small isolated speck with visible space around it.
If several dark pixels touch into an elongated smear, irregular patch, or connected cluster, emit one dark_mark for that connected area instead of splitting it into spots.
localization: BBOX MUST enclose the FULL visible footprint of the dark spot or connected spot cluster, plus a small margin - not just one or two dark pixels and not the whole face.
One coherent blemish area gets ONE box; do not split a single speck/cluster into tiny pixel-sized boxes.
The box is usually small - typically well under ~0.15 of the image in each dimension - but it must cover the actual discolored area and its visible texture.
NEVER draw a box that spans a large fraction of the face or reaches unrelated areas.
The marker segments the dark pixels inside this bbox, so make the box defect-sized, not pixel-sized.

discreteness.meaning: a DISCRETE rounded spot with a clear boundary vs diffuse haze (1.0 = crisp spot; low = vague mottling).

darkness.meaning: how much darker than the surrounding finish (1.0 = clearly darker).

not_tint_certainty.meaning: confidence it is not tint / a hole bore or its shadow / specular glare.

white_mark.signature: A localised irregular PALE, dull, low-lustre patch where the underlying brushed/machining grain is still visible through it - a loss of shine/colour, NOT added dark debris. Distinguish from glare and from dark burns/speckling (which are darker than the surroundings).
disambiguation: DECISIVE TEST vs glare: a white_mark is LESS reflective than the metal around it (a dull, flat, matte patch - luster is LOST, and the brushed grain stays visible through it, and it does NOT move/shift with viewing angle).

GLARE/specular highlight is MORE reflective than its surroundings (a bright mirror-like hotspot that washes out the grain and sits where light bounces off - typically a smooth gradient near an edge or high point).
If the patch is brighter and grain-free -> glare, ignore it.
If the patch is duller/flatter than the rest of the same face with grain still readable -> white_mark.

When a part has an overall dull/rainbow passivation tint that covers the WHOLE face uniformly, that is the finish, not a white_mark; only flag a LOCALISED dull patch that contrasts with the rest of the same face.
actionability_rule: A coherent localized matte/pale patch with a visible footprint and contrast against the surrounding finish is actionable as white_mark even when it is irregular or moderately large.
Box the full visible patch with a small margin; do not reduce it to tiny bright pixels or dismiss it as glare when the brushed grain remains visible.

logo_missing.signature: A required embossed, stamped or printed logo / part-marking is absent, incomplete or illegible where the golden reference shows it present. Only checked for parts that declare a logo (opt-in).
